extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is a letter-format secondary analysis of a parent RCT (Méndez-Flores et al. 2022, doi:10.1002/ctm2.763). No per-arm means, SDs, or individual numeric outcome values are reported in the text — only p-value thresholds (p<0.01, p<0.05) for between-group differences. All quantitative biomarker data appear only in supplementary figures (Figures S2-S5) and supplementary tables (Tables S2-S4) which are not included in this text. The network correlation values (rho=0.17, rho=0.36) are reported for male vs female PTIC subgroups only, not as between-arm comparisons. No primary outcome is explicitly designated; all outcomes are biomarker-based (cytokines, chemokines, blood count ratios, physiological network properties). No patient-reported outcomes, clinical outcomes, or adverse events are reported. The analysis focuses on 37 completers (20 PTIC, 17 placebo) from the original 89 randomized, representing very high attrition (~58%). This paper is very poorly suited for quantitative meta-analysis due to absence of extractable numeric effect sizes.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Table 2 reports baseline values as mean ± SE (labeled as SD in table header but confirmed as SE from GEE model context). Table 4 values labeled as mean ± SD in header but likely SE from GEE estimated means given the very small values relative to expected SDs for gait parameters. The 8-week unblinded crossover phase was not analyzed due to high attrition. Between-group effect for BPI-I CI appears to favor IG but CI notation (-4.543, 0.689) may indicate the CI crosses zero or may reflect an error in the original table. Five participants discontinued during the blinded phase but individual-level dropout reasons by arm were not fully detailed (flow chart referenced but image removed). The paper design is partially single-blind as investigators were unblinded. Baseline BPI-I was significantly different between groups (p=0.021), which is a notable limitation.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Table 3 (repeated measures ANOVA results) was severely garbled in the extraction — cells appear merged and misaligned, making it impossible to reliably extract all F-statistics and p-values by outcome from that table. Key statistics were extracted from the Results text instead. Per-arm means and SDs at T1 and T2 are NOT reported in the paper for any outcome except baseline (Table 2); post-treatment values appear only in figures (log-transformed). The MFIS-physical post hoc effect sizes (Cohen's d) were verbatim: active T0 vs T1 d=1.032, T0 vs T2 d=0.833; sham T0 vs T1 d=0.282, T0 vs T2 d=0.266. The BDI-II post hoc effect sizes: active T0 vs T1 d=0.625, T0 vs T2 d=0.567; sham T0 vs T1 d=0.235, T0 vs T2 d=0.844. MFIS-total change scores reported narratively: active group mean reduction 9.8 points at T1, sham 7.7 points — these are approximate narrative values, not extracted as formal arm_results due to lack of accompanying SDs. Stroop individual trial scores (W, C, CW) baseline also reported in Table 2 but not extracted as separate outcomes. SDMT baseline data reported (active: 31.08±10.56; sham: 34.70±11.62) but SDMT was not a primary/secondary outcome in the trial and not followed up. The between_group_effects interaction p-values for time×group are: MFIS-total p=0.184, MFIS-physical p=0.034, MFIS-cognitive not significant, MFIS-psychosocial not significant, BDI-II p=0.036, EuroQol-5D p=0.120, Stroop not significant.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. This is a crossover trial: Group 1 received active (Formula C) in Period 1 (day 0-28) then open-label active in Period 2 (day 28-56). Group 2 received placebo (hempseed oil with unexpected therapeutic terpenes) in Period 1 then open-label active in Period 2. The placebo was contaminated with terpenes, making it an active comparator rather than true placebo. 2. Table 3 and Table 4 report within-group paired comparisons only. No formal between-group effect sizes (mean differences with CIs or p-values) are reported in tables; between-group comparisons described narratively only (Table 4 header missing Group 2 Day 56 column label in source). 3. Between-group mean differences at day 28 were calculated from Table 3 arm means (arm1_mean - arm2_mean). 4. Table 4 (Group 1 within-group differences) reports difference in means and SDs for paired tests; p-values reported one-tailed. Key significant findings for Group 1: dyspnea p=0.013, anxiety p=0.006, sleep disturbance p=0.041 (day 0 vs day 28). 5. Table 5 (Group 2, day 28 vs day 56 differences) reports marginal significance for dyspnea p=0.096, anxiety p=0.066. 6. PGIC scored as non-normally distributed; Wilcoxon signed rank used; p<0.005 for Group 1 day 0 vs day 28, p<0.05 for Group 1 day 0 vs day 56, p<0.05 for Group 2 day 28 vs day 56. 7. Demographics table labels arms as 'Full-active (n=12)' and 'Part-active (n=11)' corresponding to completers, not randomized totals. 8. The N=13 for Group 1 PGIC at day 0 (vs N=12 for other measures) may reflect one additional participant who completed baseline PGIC but not other measures. 9. COVID-19 Employment Change Questionnaire administered but results not reported quantitatively in the paper. 10. Some table rendering in the source was garbled (Table 4 difference columns merged/unclear); values extracted from readable portions.

For outcomes 14 (GDS) and 15 (PSS), between-group effect_value was calculated as adjusted mean change rehab minus adjusted mean change control: GDS = -2.39 - 2.68 = -5.07; PSS = -2.46 - 3.26 = -5.72. Critical limitation: The ANOVA tables (Tables 1 and 2) report only sum of squares, df, mean squares, F-statistics, and p-values for between-group comparisons. extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is a non-randomized quasi-experimental study (single-arm + external control), not an RCT. The paper reports Hodges-Lehmann estimator as 'Difference' (not a simple mean difference), and all central tendency values are medians with IQRs; no means or SDs are reported for outcomes. The effect_value in between_group_effects fields has been populated with the Hodges-Lehmann estimator as reported. Baseline pulmonary function and 6-MWD data were unavailable (stated as limitation). Per-arm n_analyzed at each timepoint varies and was not fully tabulated in the paper (only aggregated numbers in Figure 1). The lung imaging relative-change data appear primarily in Figure 2 for most timepoints; only the day-90 ground-glass lesion comparison for severe patients had quantitative values explicitly reported in text. Total lesion proportion and solid component change data for moderate patients and total lesion proportion for severe patients were mentioned but numeric per-arm results not provided in text (only in Figure 2). Symptoms (pain, appetite loss, sleep difficulties) and SF-36 data referenced in Supplementary Table 1; D-dimer and IL-6 follow-up data referenced in Supplementary Table 2 — these supplementary tables were not included in the provided paper text. Omitted outcomes (data only in figures or supplementary): total lesion proportion change, solid component change, incidence of pain, incidence of appetite loss, incidence of sleep difficulties, SF-36 scores, D-dimer levels, IL-6 levels at follow-up.

Follow-up at 7 months and 9 months had binary/categorical outcome data for some measures (Activities of daily living limitation, Doing exercise, Presenting symptoms, Returning to work) which are not separately extracted as outcomes here due to complex nested table structure. GRC follow-up means extracted from Table 2 partial data. Per-arm means and SDs for PedsQL GI scores and spike antigen concentrations are not reported as numbers in text — data only in figures. Spearman correlations reported: IFNgamma vs spike antigen r=0.37, p=0.004; IL-6 vs spike antigen r=0.67, p<0.001; GI symptoms vs spike antigen r=-0.5, p=0.003. Fisher's exact p-values for GI recovery at day 7 and day 14 stated as p<0.001. Irritability continuous comparison by t-test p=0.01 also reported. Outcomes 7, 8, 9 (cytokines, antibodies) have no per-arm quantitative data in text — data only in figures. The effect_measure for binary Fisher's exact comparisons is listed as odds_ratio as a placeholder since no OR was explicitly calculated; the paper reports only p-values from Fisher's exact test without effect sizes. n_analyzed for spike antigen outcomes refers to the subset with spike antigen detected at enrollment (5 larazotide, 3-4 placebo).

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. Table 4 baseline N values inferred from Table 1 (N=274 usual care, N=270 intervention) minus missing counts per outcome. Follow-up N values (n=200 usual care, n=210 intervention) taken from text and CONSORT diagram. For EQ-5D-5L index and VAS, exact follow-up per-arm n values were inferred by subtracting missing counts from the 3-month follow-up totals (missing: index - 6 intervention, 6 usual care; VAS - 4 intervention, 10 usual care). For GSE scales, 1 missing in usual care at follow-up was noted. For SF-12, 1 missing at baseline in intervention. The paper reports two adjusted models for all outcomes (Model A: adjusted for baseline + site random effect; Model B: additionally adjusted for age, gender, ethnic group, employment status, number of long covid symptoms); both sets of between-group estimates are extracted. The p_value_exact for FIS overall score Model A is set to false because the paper states p<0.001. The 6-week follow-up data were collected for health economic evaluation purposes only and are not reported numerically in the paper. The acceptability/appropriateness/feasibility implementation measures (Table 2) are not extracted as outcomes per se but are noted. The binary responder analysis (odds ratio for achieving MID on primary outcome) is noted: unadjusted OR 1.40 (0.94-2.09), fully adjusted OR 1.46 (0.95-2.25), not extracted as a separate outcome object since it derives from the primary outcome.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. Several values required careful disambiguation. Table 3 reports between-group p-values in the 't' and 'p' columns and within-group p-values in 'tb'/'pa' (paired) and 'Z'/'pa' (Wilcoxon) columns. The FSS post-treatment SD for taVNS group appears as '5.05 ± 0.10' in the results text but '5.05 ± 1.10' in Table 3 — Table 3 value used as the text value of 0.10 appears to be a typographical error. The between-group p-value for FSS at post-treatment in Table 3 is p=0.034 but the abstract states p=0.022; Table 4 (pre-post change score comparison) reports p=0.022 for FSS, so both values extracted separately. The 'pre-and post-test' comparison in Table 4 represents change-score differences between arms (delta taVNS minus delta sham). For LF power in Table 4, the baseline difference is reported as −123.4 ± 30.5 and post as −53 ± 90.28 with delta −70.4 ± 71.12; these represent taVNS-minus-sham delta values and p=0.029. The HF power between-group p=0.042 (from abstract/Table 4) refers to the change-score comparison, not the endpoint comparison. Cohen's d and Hedges' g values are reported verbatim in the paper for between-group comparisons but not extracted as separate fields per schema. The FSS post-treatment between_group_effects has two entries: one for the endpoint comparison (p=0.034 from Table 3) and one for the change-score comparison (p=0.022 from Table 4). The sham taVNS group baseline HF power SD of 80.67 seems anomalously large compared to the mean of 29.70 — extracted verbatim as reported.

(4) Sheetali gender listed as '17/1' in table (likely typo for 17/13); percent female calculated as 43.3% based on reasonable interpretation. (5) Bhramari baseline RMSSD listed as '273' in table — interpreted as 27.3 ms. (6) Between-group effect sizes (mean differences) for FVC, FEV1, PEFR, RMSSD stated in text but without CIs; p-values stated as thresholds only. (7) No control arm post-intervention values reported for any outcome. (8) The paper states interventions were '15 minutes twice daily' in the abstract but '30-minute sessions daily' in the methods — an internal inconsistency noted. extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. EVA (VAS) control group post-intervention value of 40.20 ± 0.63 appears to be a data error in the table (likely should be 4.0 or similar; the before value was 0.20 ± 0.63 and the p-value for between groups was 0.085 suggesting no significant difference). This value has been extracted verbatim as printed. 2. The p-value column labels in Table 2 refer to: A*G = interaction (time x group), A = time effect (within group across both groups), G = group effect (between groups). The between_group_effects p_values reported here use the G (group) column where available, and A (time) column for intragroup effects reported as significant. For SF-36 Physical Functioning: G p=0.034 is reported as between-group; for SF-36 Role Physical: A p=0.046 is the within-group (time) effect; for SF-36 Pain: A p=0.021 is within-group; for handgrip: A p=0.029 is within-group. These distinctions are noted as the table structure uses three p-value columns (A*G, A, G). 3. The calculated between-group mean differences at endpoint are approximate as the p-values in the G column represent group main effects from repeated-measures ANOVA, not simple endpoint differences. 4. Age data reported only as categorical ranges (n, %), not as continuous mean/SD. 5. Intervention duration varied from 10 to 40 sessions (most between 5-8 weeks), control assessed at 8 weeks.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Study is a quasi-experimental matched comparative prospective study, not a true RCT — no randomization described. Table 2 shows denominator of 29 for some G1 outcomes (dry cough, dyspnea n%, chest pain n%, fatigue n%) despite G1 n=30, and denominator of 9 for G2 outcomes despite G2 n=12 — this inconsistency is unexplained in the text and may represent missing data at those timepoints. Means reported without SDs for most continuous outcomes in Table 3 except 6-MWD. Between-group factorial ANOVA F and p values are reported in Table 3 and extracted as between_group_effects p_values where they appear to represent the group-by-time interaction; however the abstract reports percent-change comparisons (e.g. FEV1 p=0.005) which differ from the Table 3 ANOVA p-values — the Table 3 values are used here as they are more directly extractable. The abstract states between-group comparisons for FEV1 p=0.005, FVC p=0.003, TLC p<0.001, DLCO p<0.001, 6-MWD p=0.015, but these appear to be based on percentage change comparisons not shown in Table 3; these values are NOT reflected in the Table 3 Factorial ANOVA column. PI max higher_is_better set to false since more negative values indicate greater inspiratory strength, making interpretation ambiguous; values reported as negative in table. The overall baseline 6-MWD reported in text as 485.68m±119 does not match per-arm values (466±139 for G1, 526±50 for G2), suggesting overall figure is a weighted average.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. This paper embeds an RCT (n=18) within a 2-year observational follow-up study (n=30). JSON extraction focuses on the RCT component. The sham arm baseline IQR for sniff nasal pressure % predicted shows '290.0' as upper bound for post-training (table value appears to be a data entry error in the paper; extracted verbatim). The observational 2-year follow-up data (e.g., twPdi change from 14 to 31 months) are reported in online supplement Tables E2 and E3 and not fully available in the main text for extraction. Several outcomes (CRQ mastery, CRQ emotional function, CMS twPes, CMS twPgas, CMS MRR/MCR normalized, TH10 twPgas, Sniff Pes, Mueller Pdi, Mueller Pes, Valsalva Pgas, Cough Pgas) are reported in Table 2 with full data but were omitted from the outcomes array to manage response length; all showed non-significant between-group differences. Six-week post-IMT follow-up data are in supplemental Table E5 and not extractable from the main text. The paper uses medians and IQRs throughout (non-normal distributions); no means or SDs are available. Arm_id=1 is IMT treatment; arm_id=2 is sham control. The between-group p-value of 0.03 for Borg and DVAI are stated in the abstract with specific reference to between-group comparison (sham vs IMT), whereas the Table 2 between-group p-values are 0.24 and 0.56 respectively — the abstract values appear to be within-group p-values mislabeled; within-group p-values (0.03 for IMT arm Borg, 0.03 for DVAI in IMT arm) match Table 2. The between-group p-values from Table 2 are used for between_group_effects.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Per-arm means and SDs for outcome trajectories (VAS slopes, EEG power slopes) were not reported in tables or text - only F-statistics, p-values, and effect sizes (partial eta-squared) for the LMM main effects and interactions were provided. Specific raw per-arm means/SDs for AX-CPT behavioral and EEG outcomes are data only in figures. The between-group effect for occipital alpha (outcome 7) is a post-hoc comparison mean difference of 0.06 (sham > verum at post-assessment) with d=0.33, 95% CI [0.07, 0.59], p=0.011 (FDR-corrected). The primary outcome of this paper is subjective state fatigue (VAS slopes); the trial's primary outcome (trait fatigue measured by questionnaires) was reported in a companion paper (Mischke & Zaehle, Brain Stimulation, 2025). The gamified Go/No-Go task was not pre-registered. P50 analysis had reduced n (verum n=19, sham n=16 at pre/post; verum n=18, sham n=15 at follow-up) due to 5 exclusions. The occipital alpha interaction (stimulation x assessment) was significant at F(2,74.45)=4.18, p=0.020, partial eta2=0.10; the sham group showed stronger alpha increase at post vs verum (mean difference=0.06, p=0.011, d=0.33) and reduction from post to follow-up in sham (mean difference=0.05, p=0.010, d=0.35). D-prime in Go/No-Go showed significant stimulation condition main effect (F(1,49)=6.22, p=0.016, partial eta2=0.11) and session x condition interaction (F(3,110.20)=5.57, p=0.001). EQ-5D-5L Index also reported: verum M=0.64 SD=0.26, sham M=0.69 SD=0.28, p=0.562.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: The paper reports the primary outcome primarily as categorical (complete vs. partial vs. no taste restoration) rather than continuous — no continuous per-arm means/SDs are reported for the taste outcome itself. The between-group comparison for 'taste restored after one month' (p=0.041) appears to refer to the overall distribution difference (complete vs. partial), while p<0.001 refers specifically to complete restoration in Group I vs. partial in Group II. For outcome_id 2 (complete restoration at 4 weeks), the control arm events (11/18 = 61.1%) were calculated as: 18 total minus 7 partial = 11 with complete restoration, assuming the remaining patients had complete rather than no restoration — this inference may not be exact as the text does not clearly state zero cases of no restoration in Group II at 4 weeks. Intermediate timepoints (2-week and 3-week) have no numeric data reported in text or tables — data may only be in Figure 2a. Table 4 (cost-effectiveness results) had heavily merged/garbled cells in the source text; arm-level adjusted cost values (REGAIN £1987 CI 1666-2307; usual care £1681 CI 1406-1955) and QALY values were extracted from partially reconstructed table. The 6-month CI upper bound for EQ-5D utility in Table 3 appears to be a typo (0.67 instead of likely 0.067) — extracted verbatim. Intervention cost per patient: REGAIN £399.92 (n=298); usual care £72.71 (n=287). Resource use cost breakdown by category (medication, outpatient, community care, A&E, inpatient, PSS, nursing home) extracted in Table 2 with complete data across 0-12 months. No adverse events data reported in this economic paper. Time since hospital discharge to randomisation mean 10.6 months reported overall only.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is a post-hoc analysis of a primary RCT (NCT05047952; primary paper: McIntyre et al., Brain, 2023). The DSST baseline values are reported as combined z-scores. The between-group mean difference of 0.621 (SE=0.313, p=0.047) is from GEE adjusted model moderated by CRP/TG-HDL/BMI — it reflects the interaction-moderated comparison, not a simple overall between-group difference. Week 2 DSST data were collected but no numeric values reported for that timepoint in this paper. Endpoint absolute DSST scores (week 8) not reported — only change-from-baseline values available. The vortioxetine arm TRG-HDL SD (17.19) appears anomalously large compared to placebo (0.99), likely reflecting skewed data or outliers. Adverse events not reported in this post-hoc analysis paper. BMI sub-category means reported in Table 1 but reflect subgroup means within weight categories rather than overall summary statistics.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: The paper reports between-group effects as Beta-coefficients from a Univariate General Linear Model adjusted for age and BMI; these are interpreted as adjusted mean differences (intervention minus control) for absolute change scores. Note that positive Beta-coefficient for PSQI and HADS-Anxiety indicates improvement in the BT group (i.e., the control group worsened or improved less, and the BT group had greater improvement in change scores — the directionality is: positive beta = BT group improved more, for scales where lower=better; negative beta = BT group improved more for scales where higher=better). Per-arm follow-up means and SDs for timepoints 2 and 3 are not provided in tables — only absolute change from baseline means are shown in figures (as mean with SE bars) without numeric values in the text or supplemental tables referenced. Therefore, endpoint values at timepoints 2 and 3 per arm could not be extracted. The paper states data are expressed as mean (SE) in figures but exact values are not provided. The RR data for improvement categorization (e.g., SF-36 pain RR=2.8 [1.69;4.64], energy/fatigue RR=2.0 [1.31;3.05]) are reported as supplemental figure data and not extracted as separate outcomes. Table 1 missing the BT group column header for sample sizes (table appears to show only Control N=47 in header but BT group data is present). ICU admission rates are provided (BT: 3.9%, Control: 2.1%) but not used to calculate percent previously hospitalized as ICU is a subset. Baseline PSQI SD for control arm listed with comma decimal '11.13 (4,17)' — extracted as 4.17.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. This is a non-randomized, open-label dose-escalation study with historical control (not an RCT). The 'control' is a historical placebo showing 5.9% improvement on Chalder Likert from Cho et al. 2005 meta-analysis — no concurrent placebo arm exists. 2. All outcome data are reported as percentage change from baseline on a normalized 0-100% scale; absolute scores (raw means and SDs at each timepoint) are NOT reported in the paper. Therefore sd, se, ci_95_low, ci_95_high for arm_results are null throughout. 3. The paper reports FSS and PROMIS-7a results only for Long COVID arms (arms 4 and 5); ME/CFS arm FSS and PROMIS results are not reported in accessible tabular or numeric form. 4. Adverse event data for ME/CFS arms 1 and 2 reference '1000 mg BID group' with n=24 in the text but the arm enrolled N=29; the text says '2/24 in the 1000 mg BID group' which may be an error or refer to a subset — extracted verbatim. 5. The Long COVID 500 mg BID arm (arm 4) Chalder Bimodal 2-week value shown in Table 3 as '46.8%***' appears under the '6-Weeks' row for bimodal — Table 3 Long COVID section header reads '2-Weeks' and '6-Weeks' for Chalder Fatigue at 6 Weeks columns; the table is somewhat garbled/merged. Values extracted as best interpretation from text and table. 6. p-values reported only as thresholds (* p<0.05, ** p<0.005, *** p<0.0005 or similar); no exact p-values provided. 7. Baseline Chalder scores described as ranging 76-92% of maximum but no per-arm breakdown given. 8. ME/CFS arm age (median 47) and sex (73.7% female) reported for the group overall, not per arm. Long COVID demographics not reported. 9. The 'Insomnia' AE is reported as '1/26 in the 500 mg BID group' in text but arm 1 enrolled N=23 — possible text error; extracted with n=1 for arm 1.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. Table 1 baseline data is reported for N=134 (67 per arm), but Table 2 uses N=62 per arm (per-protocol completers). extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: The paper states outcome reassessment was done 'after 4 weeks of the treatment' but the treatment duration was 2 months (8 weeks, twice weekly). It is unclear whether the post-injection QOD-NS was assessed at 4 weeks into treatment or at the end of the 8-week treatment course. weeks_from_randomization for the post-treatment timepoint is set to 4 weeks per the explicit text but this may underestimate total follow-up. Table 3 contains merged/complex header rows; the QOD-NS post values for Group B show median listed in a combined 'Median / Minimum' merged cell (4.50 / 0.00 for Group A and 7.00 / 2.00 for Group B) — values extracted are consistent with Table 2 and the narrative. The baseline 'complain' data in Table 3 (Group A: 14 anosmia / 6 hyposmia; Group B: 18 anosmia / 2 hyposmia) reflects presenting complaint, while post-treatment 'effect' counts (arm1: 1 anosmia, 2 hyposmia, 17 normosmia; arm2: 3 anosmia, 5 hyposmia, 12 normosmia) are the follow-up outcomes. The between-group effect_value for QOD-NS post is calculated as arm1_mean minus arm2_mean = 7.60 - 12.40 = -4.80 (negative = arm1 better, consistent with lower score = better). Within-group pre-to-post p-values are both <0.001 (Wilcoxon signed-rank test). No objective olfactory testing data available.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is a 6-month follow-up study of the HENIVOT RCT, not a long COVID intervention trial per se. The population is ICU survivors of acute COVID-19 hypoxemic respiratory failure assessed for long-term outcomes. The study design arm sizes differ between primary paper (N=54 helmet, N=55 HFNC randomized) and follow-up completion (N=35 helmet, N=36 HFNC). Note: Table 2 headers show N=31 helmet and N=33 HFNC for symptoms, N=30 each for pulmonary function, and N=35/N=36 for quality of life sections — these varying Ns are preserved in arm_results. The 30-s chair stand test p-value (0.65) is reported but no between-group effect size or CI is provided. The EQ-VAS high-flow group IQR in Table 2 has a formatting issue (value '[60-80]' appears on next line); extracted as median=70, IQR 60-80 based on text and table. Outcomes from Table 3 (intubated vs non-intubated subgroup) are captured in subgroup_analyses rather than as separate outcome entries to avoid duplication. Additional outcomes not extracted as separate objects due to space: maximal mid-expiratory flow 25-75 (MEF25-75), alveolar ventilation volume, residual volume/TLC ratio, FEV1<80% binary, FEV1/FVC<80% binary, TLC<80% binary, residual volume<80% binary, 6MWT interruption, 6MWT unable to walk predicted distance, various minor symptoms (dry cough, sore throat, rhinitis, smell disorder, taste disorder, dizziness, myalgia, chest pain, sicca syndrome, inappetence, diarrhoea, decreased visual acuity). Laboratory test results (hemoglobin, platelets, WBC, bilirubin, transaminases, creatinine, BUN, eGFR) reported in supplemental tables not available in main text.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1) All per-arm values in Table 2 are reported as mean (95% CI) — no SDs available for any secondary outcome; means are the midpoints of the CIs but are not explicitly stated as single numbers (only CIs given); means were taken as the stated central value where provided (e.g. 9.73, 8.97 etc. for PHQ-9). 2) ISWT primary outcome: per-arm means at baseline and follow-up are reported only as mean (95% CI) from the GLMM marginal means, not raw group means with SDs. For arm 1 baseline: midpoint of 219-351=285m; post: midpoint of 244-380=312m. For arm 2 baseline: midpoint of 296-411=353m; post: midpoint of 334-442=388m. Change-from-baseline means were calculated from these midpoints (27m and 35m respectively). 3) Table 2 participant counts: the table header states Face-to-face=56, Remote=62, Usual care=63 (note: these differ slightly from randomization numbers of 56, 63, 62 — the Usual care and Remote appear swapped in the table header vs results text; extracted as stated in table). 4) Immune substudy (Table 3): CD4+ n=8 (face-to-face) and n=15 (usual care); CD8+ n=10 and n=16; NK n=10 and n=16; Total lymphocytes n=13 and n=18. extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: CRITICAL DATA QUALITY ISSUES: (1) All quantitative data appear only in bar chart figures (Figs 1-5); no tables provided. Percentages are reported verbatim in the results text, but exact n per subgroup are not stated — event counts were back-calculated from stated percentages assuming equal subgroup sizes within each disorder type across the two arms. However, the per-subgroup ns are uncertain: summing inferred subgroup ns (15+23+25+17+25=105) exceeds stated arm 1 total of 80, so the subgroup assignments are not additive across the whole arm (i.e., participants may have had only one disorder type per arm, and the per-subgroup n may represent only that subgroup, not the full arm). The inferred n per subgroup (e.g., 15 per arm for polymenorrhea based on 13.3% = ~2/15) is speculative. (2) No baseline demographic data (age, BMI, time since infection) reported per arm. (3) Allocation method not described — this is NOT a confirmed RCT; described as a controlled study without randomization details. (4) Follow-up duration stated as 3-6 months post-treatment but exact treatment duration not specified. (5) The Ukrainian-language abstract reverses group numbering (group 1 = standard, group 2 = modified) relative to the English text (group 1 = modified, group 2 = standard) — extraction follows English text convention. (6) Adverse event percentages given as ranges (e.g., 15-20%, 60-70%) without exact denominators.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. Crossover design: all 20 participants completed both arms. Per-arm n=20 for all outcomes (each participant contributed data to both conditions). Baseline values for each arm reflect participants at entry into that condition (post-washout values used as pre for second condition). The paper reports intervention x time p-values from two-way ANOVA in Table 2 — these are used as between-group p-values. Calculated between-group mean differences are endpoint post-treatment differences (arm1 post minus arm2 post), which reflects the crossover contrast available from Table 2. The paper's primary between-group p-values (from delta of change comparisons via paired t-test) are: 6MWT p=0.02, TUG p=0.002, Barthel p=0.02; these are reported as between_group_effects p_values. For other outcomes, the intervention x time interaction p-value from two-way ANOVA is used as the between-group p-value. Training cardiopulmonary monitoring data (SpO2, HR, systolic/diastolic BP) appear only as figures with summary statistics in text — these are not extracted as formal outcomes. The 95% CI values in Table 2 are for Hedge's g effect sizes, not for mean differences; they are not entered into the between_group_effects CI fields. Note: the paper states TUG delta-of-change p=0.002 in the results text (Fig 3E) despite the two-way ANOVA intervention x time p=0.01 — the paired t-test p=0.002 is used as the primary between-group comparison. Sequence effects were significant for MRC, PCFS, MoCA, and Barthel Index, indicating potential carryover.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. The paper reports almost all quantitative outcomes as percent change from baseline only, without providing absolute pre/post values or SDs — this severely limits effect size extraction. Absolute values are provided only for 6MWT baseline (median with IQR per arm) and overall FEV1 baseline (median IQR pooled). 2. Psychological and cognitive outcome data (Table 1) are reported only as Wilcoxon Z statistics and p-values across all rehabilitation groups combined, with no per-arm means/SDs. 3. Allostatic load is reported as categorical distribution (% in each severity category) before and after, not as continuous scores per arm. 4. The note in the abstract vs methods section reverses the group numbering (abstract English version lists groups differently from methods). We followed the methods section: arm1=whirlpool/hydromassage, arm2=Biolong baths, arm3=NaCl mineral baths, arm4=control. 5. Between-group effects are not directly reported; the paper reports only within-arm pre/post changes with p-values from Wilcoxon tests. No between-group inferential statistics are provided. 6. Several figures referenced (Figs 1, 2, 3) contain allostatic load distribution data that supplements text; extracted from text descriptions. 7. Omitted outcomes due to lack of any quantitative data: superoxide dismutase, sinus tachycardia/bradycardia rates (reported as percent of group but not per-arm post values with statistics), all complaint frequency outcomes (narrative percent only). 8. The Schulte Tables Efficiency of Work subscale did not reach significance (Z=-1.9, p=0.064) and is noted but all data remain null.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. This study is NOT an RCT; it is an open-label quasi-experimental comparative study with no described randomization. design_type set to quasi-experimental. 2. Baseline imbalances exist: fatigue severity (experimental 2.65 vs control 2.31, p=0.0001) and sleep disorder severity (1.70 vs 1.00, p=0.04) differ significantly at baseline, complicating interpretation. 3. Table 3 p-values are reported as combined pairs (e.g., '0.0001/0.02') where the first value appears to refer to Day 1 between-group comparison and the second to Day 5; this notation is ambiguous and has been interpreted accordingly. 4. For FAS/chronic fatigue outcome (Table 4), only binary classification (above/below threshold of 22) is reported, not continuous FAS scores; no p-value is reported for the between-group comparison at Day 10 (text states 'no statistically significant differences'). 5. The symptom severity scale means in Table 3 are computed across all participants in each group (including those without the symptom, who presumably score 1), not only those with the symptom present. 6. Additional binary outcomes fully extracted from Table 2 but not individually listed as outcomes: shortness of breath, cough, dizziness, chest pain, loss of taste, perverted smell, perverted taste, sleep disorder, anxiety, hair loss, abdominal pain — all had complete n/% data at days 1/5/10. The most clinically important (loss of smell, headache, joint pain, fatigue) are included. 7. The paper notes that 100% of experimental group participants had fatigue and dizziness at all timepoints per Table 2 (binary), though the severity scores improved — this creates an apparent contradiction with Table 3 severity data.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. The Schober test is measured in two parts: 'initial' measurement (always 15.00 ± 0.00 cm for both groups/timepoints, as this is the fixed starting mark) and 'final' measurement (the actual flexion endpoint). The 'difference' is the clinically meaningful value. The lateral inclination tests measure the distance from fingertip to floor and are reported similarly in three components: initial (standing upright finger-to-floor), final (in flexion finger-to-floor), and difference. No exact p-values were reported for between-group comparisons at post-intervention — only p<0.05 thresholds with footnote annotations in Table 3. The G2 pain increase was stated as statistically significant (intragroup p<0.05) in the results text. The Schober final measurement and difference were significantly greater in G1 vs G2 at both pre- and post-intervention (p<0.05 between groups). The Stibor final measurement was significantly greater in G1 vs G2 only at pre-intervention. No between-group significance was reported for grip strength or lateral flexion. The analysis used the randomized N (G1=20, G2=19) despite 11 dropouts, suggesting intent-to-treat or the table reports randomized n rather than analyzed n — this is ambiguous. Percent female for G1 calculated as 11/20=55%; for G2 as 16/19=84.2%.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. The paper labels the post-intervention timepoint as 'T16' referring to the 16th session (not 16 weeks); actual duration is 8 weeks. Cirtometry IM (inspiratory max) and EM (expiratory max) absolute values at axial, mamilar, and basal levels were also reported in Table 3 but only the difference (IM-EM) showed significant within-group changes in GP; absolute IM and EM values extracted only for basal EM (which showed intragroup significance in GP). Intragroup p-values and 95% CIs for the GP 6MWT total distance improvement: CI95% -102.576 to -42.723, p=0.000; for 6MWT 2-4 min: CI95% -45.978 to -10.521, p=0.003; for 6MWT 4-6 min: CI95% -52.838 to -11.961, p=0.004. Intragroup p-values for GC manovacuometry: MIP CI95% -21.562 to -6.086, p=0.001; MEP CI95% -20.432 to -5.181, p=0.002. Intragroup for GP axial cirtometry difference: CI95% -3.104 to -0.695, p=0.004; mamilar: CI95% -2.441 to -0.658, p=0.002; basal: CI95% -2.509 to -0.290, p=0.024; basal EM: CI95% 0.272 to 3.527, p=0.016. Cirtometry absolute IM and EM values at axial and mamilar levels (non-significant) were present in table but omitted from outcomes to keep within size limits. The 95% CIs reported in the text for intragroup differences were not extracted as between-group effects; only the between-group comparison for Borg 5-min post-6MWT had verbatim CI and p-value. extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Paper is in Russian with an English abstract. The post-treatment CRP value of 2.5±3.4 mg/L is reported as an average across both groups combined ('снижался в обеих группах и составил в среднем 2.5±3.4 мг/л'), so the same value was applied to both arms with result_source='inferred'. The table (Table 2) shows CRP 2.5±3.4 only in the 'after treatment' column for group 1 and the same value for group 2, consistent with the combined average. The p-value of <0.001 is applied to all outcomes from Table 2 row; individual between-group p-values are not separately reported per outcome. The study reports adverse events for both groups combined (26% of 103 = ~27 patients) mostly attributable to corticosteroids (skin dryness/acne, hyperglycemia), not broken down by arm. The 6-minute walk test is listed as an assessment tool in the methods but no quantitative results are reported in the results section. Quality of life is mentioned (75 points out of 100 at baseline) but no post-treatment value is given numerically per arm, so it was omitted as a separate outcome. The time_since_infection_months values were calculated from the reported days: Group 1: 46.7/30=1.56 months (SD: 13.1/30=0.44); Group 2: 48.7/30=1.62 months (SD: 14.1/30=0.47). Percent female calculated: Group 1 had 49 men out of 53 = 4 women = 7.5% female; Group 2 had 47 men out of 50 = 3 women = 6.0% female. The study was funded by pharmaceutical company Solofarma (manufacturer of Trecresan); authors received a grant. No trial registration number reported.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: CRITICAL: Primary outcome data (VAS pain, Lequesne index) at day 50 are presented ONLY in figures (Fig. 1) with no numeric values in text or tables — only p-values and U-test statistics are reported (VAS: U-test=5.71, p<0.0001; Lequesne: U-test=6.32, p<0.0001). Per-arm means/medians/SDs at follow-up for these outcomes are not extractable. Similarly, inflammatory biomarkers (CRP, IL-6, IL-1β, D-dimer, fibrinogen) are shown in Figures 2 and 3 without numeric values in text — only significance levels and within-group p-values are stated. The BMI values in Table 1 are medians with IQR (arm1: 26.5 [24;31.2], arm2: 28 [26.4;29.4]). Baseline VAS medians from Table 1 were extracted successfully. extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: CRITICAL DATA QUALITY ISSUES: (1) Table 5 (HRQOL Parameters Before and After Treatment) reports data ONLY for the insulin/intervention group — no placebo arm data is presented in this table, making between-group effect size calculation impossible for post-treatment comparisons. The p-values reported in Table 5 appear to be within-group pre-vs-post comparisons for the insulin arm only, not between-group comparisons. (2) TDI olfactory score data (primary endpoint from the prior publication, ref 12) is referenced but not reported quantitatively in this paper — only categorical baseline TDI distribution is shown in Table 3. Per-arm means and SDs for TDI are absent. (3) Figure 2 shows consequences of smell loss before and after 4 weeks for both groups, but numeric values are only in the figure (not extractable as text). (4) The n_randomized per arm is not reported — only 48 enrolled total and 20 per arm completed. It is unclear how the 8 dropouts were distributed between arms. (5) The paper does not report control group post-treatment outcomes in tabular form, severely limiting meta-analytic utility. (6) Perception of fire/smoke and emotional satisfaction outcomes shown in Figure 2 could not be extracted as values appear only in figure bars. Omitted figure-only outcomes: perception of fire/smoke, emotional satisfaction (pre/post for both groups from Figure 2).

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. This study measures electrodermal impedance via EAV (electroacupuncture according to Voll), a device/method with no established clinical validity. The outcomes are not recognized clinical endpoints for long COVID. 2. The intervention is a single-session diagnostic procedure (medicament testing), not a therapeutic intervention in the conventional sense. The 'treatment' and 'follow-up' occur within the same diagnostic session (pre-test vs post-test during the same visit). Duration fields are null as this is a within-session measurement. 3. Table 3 (positive responders) and Table 4 (negative responders) each show per-arm n, pre-test AMV mean±SD, and post-test AMV mean±SD for different meridian subsets. The n values per meridian vary because not all patients had all meridians affected. 4. Table 3 mentions 12 meridians but the text also references 'Ma' (Stomach) as one that showed restoration; however no Ma row appears in the table as extracted — likely a discrepancy in the paper. 5. Between-group p-values were extracted as the threshold stated in table notes (*** = p<0.001 coded as 0.001, ** = p<0.01 coded as 0.01). 7. The duplicate entry for arm_id=2 in baseline_demographics.per_arm is an artifact — only one control arm exists. 8. Negative responder outcomes (Table 4): the He, Du, Pa/Mi(D), Hau, Ni, Bl meridians showed p<0.01 between groups; Al showed p<0.001 between groups; Ne showed p<0.01 between groups. These are all showing worsening (more negative drop) in the intervention arm compared to placebo for the negative-responder subgroup. 9. The study does not report conventional long COVID clinical outcomes (fatigue scores, QoL, functional status). This paper is of very limited relevance to a conventional long COVID meta-analysis.

The note in the text states 'average age 58 years in main group and 47 years in control group' which likely refers to median given Table 1 shows medians of 62 and 50 - these are approximate descriptions. Arm_id=1 is the intervention (T=therapy/dynamic inversion table); arm_id=2 is the control (R=rehabilitation/standard care). The between-group effect for the difference in changes (Table 5) was used for between_group_effects where verbatim values were available.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Critical limitation: per-arm means and SDs are NOT reported for the primary outcomes (flanker score, BDNF) at either timepoint — data appear only in figures. The overall sample resting HR mean (79.62 bpm) is also only reported for the full sample at baseline vs. normative comparison, not per arm. F-statistics and adjusted p-values are reported for group-by-session interaction effects for flanker (F(1,1)=11.69, p_adj=0.014, pe2=0.41), BDNF (F(1,1)=9.76, p_adj=0.0314, pe2=0.22), and long-term HR (F(1,1)=46.92, p_adj=0.027, pe2=0.365), and short-term HR change (t=-2.61, df=14.811, p_adj=0.04), but no per-arm means or SDs accompany these statistics. Partial eta squared is reported as effect size for ANOVA outcomes. The linear regression between BDNF change and flanker change: F=37.79, R2_adj=0.825, p_adj=0.003. Per-arm n is inferred as 10 each (20 completers, 1:1 randomization, 2 lost to follow-up from 22). Randomization arm sizes for those lost to follow-up not specified. extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is a single-group crossover study (n=20) where all participants completed all four exercise conditions (VR, no-VR, SSE-VR, 6MWT) — there are no separate randomized arms. Arm IDs are used here to represent the four conditions rather than parallel groups. The primary key comparison reported is VR vs. no-VR for dyspnea (p=0.004, t(19)=-3.269, verbatim). Overall ANOVA F-statistics are reported for each outcome across all four conditions. The 6MWT MAP value of '1,001.6 ± 8.4 mmHg' in the original text appears to be a typographical error; the value is likely 100.16 ± 8.4 mmHg and has been extracted as such. Several figures referenced in the paper contain data that are also reported in the text (HR, SpO2, dyspnea, leg fatigue). Baseline values before each condition are noted as recorded but not reported numerically in the paper text. Exercise characteristics per condition (distance, speed, duration) are extracted from Table 2. Correlations reported: handgrip vs leg fatigue at VR end (r=-0.621, p=0.003); handgrip vs leg fatigue at SSE-VR end (r=-0.450, p=0.047); handgrip vs dyspnea at SSE-VR end (r=-0.484, p=0.030); WAI vs dyspnea at baseline (r=-0.450, p=0.046); WAI vs dyspnea at VR end (r=-0.508, p=0.022); body fat vs dyspnea at SSE-VR (r=0.461, p=0.041); body fat vs 6MWT (r=-0.498, p=0.025); muscle mass vs dyspnea at SSE-VR (r=-0.466, p=0.038). extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Table 3 presents FEV1%VC and Dyspnea/Fatigue Borg scores as median [IQR]; the IQR values in the table appear to be reported as a single bracketed value (e.g., 84.3 [6.89]) — it is unclear if this represents the IQR range or a single IQR width value; extracted as median with iqr_high. The between-group effect size column in Table 3 is labeled 'Effect size d' (Cohen's d); these were verbatim for non-parametric outcomes (dyspnea, fatigue, FEV1%VC) and are stored as 'smd' in effect_measure. For 6MWT distance, the paper reports the between-group p=0.264 with effect size d=-0.411 but does not report a mean difference CI; mean difference calculated as arm1_post minus arm2_post = 558-552=6m. PSS-10 between-group mean difference calculated as 20.7-22.2=-1.5. No CONSORT flow diagram included; attrition not reported. Figure 3 referenced for 6MWT results but values are also in Table 3. The 6MWT improvement amounts mentioned in text (56.9m VR, 39.2m control) represent within-group change scores and are consistent with table data (558-502=56, 552-512=40).

domains.support: Block randomization (block size=6) was used; groups were well-balanced at baseline on all key characteristics. Allocation was performed by a designated person (MK) after baseline testing.

Participants could not be blinded to their group allocation due to the nature of the intervention. The assessor (ML) was blinded to group allocation, but performance bias from participant knowledge of group assignment cannot be ruled out.

Dropouts occurred (n=4 IG, n=4 CG from FU1 analyses with n=34 total), with analyses conducted on completers rather than ITT. Authors state dropouts did not differ on key characteristics but analyses are per-protocol.

Validated neuropsychological instruments were used. The cognitive assessor (ML) was blinded to group allocation. Patient-reported questionnaires were self-administered, with inherent susceptibility to expectation bias.
The study was registered retrospectively (not prospectively). Multiple outcomes were tested without full pre-specification of primary vs. secondary outcomes, increasing risk of selective reporting.

subgroup_analyses.variable: Disease duration moderating effect of post-COVID symptom count on memory
subgroup_analyses.results_summary: For individuals with shorter disease duration (-1 SD), no significant association between symptom count and short-delayed recall. For average disease duration, significant negative correlation (b=-0.26, p=0.012). For longer disease duration (+1 SD), stronger negative effect (b=-0.56, p<0.001). Same pattern for long-delayed recall (interaction p=0.003).

sensitivity_analyses.description: Exploratory pre-post analysis merging both groups into a combined intervention group (n=31) to increase power, with plausibility check using Friedman tests in original control group to rule out familiarity/spontaneous effects.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: KEY DESIGN NOTE: This is a waitlist-crossover RCT. The 2x2 ANCOVA results (Table 2) are the primary between-group comparisons (IG vs CG, BL to FU1, n=34 completers). The Table 3 data are from an exploratory analysis combining both groups after crossover (n=31 total trained), not a randomized comparison — these pre/post means and SDs are provided for completeness but reflect all completers pooled, not a randomized arm comparison. Per-arm SDs are NOT reported for the primary 2x2 ANCOVA results; only adjusted means (M_adj) and SEs are available. SDs for the combined pre-post analysis (Table 3) are provided for the pooled combined group only. Baseline SDs for individual arms from Table 1 are available for demographic variables (age, BMI, weight, height) but not for cognitive/psychological outcomes. The 2x3 ANCOVA interaction effects are reported in Supplementary Table 2 (not provided in full text); the 2x2 ANCOVA interaction p-values and partial eta-squared from Table 2 are extracted as between-group effect sizes. Cohen's d values from Table 3 are for the combined pre-post comparison and are extracted as 'smd' in the exploratory combined-group outcomes (outcomes 5-21 arm_results reflect the combined group). The n=31 for Table 3 is noted as 'df+1=31' from the t-test degrees of freedom. Fatigue analysis had n=28 (df=27+1). Word fluency SDs in Table 3 appear unusually small for formal-lexical (SD=1.22 and 1.43) — these are verbatim from paper. Outcomes 5-21 arm_results only have data for arm_id=1 (combined group) as the per-arm split was not reported for Table 3. The 6-month follow-up (FU2) data for within-group stability were described narratively but no per-arm means/SDs were provided for FU2 in the text.

domains.support: Explicitly described as a non-randomized study; allocation was made arbitrarily based on patient sports and computer equipment availability.
Open-label design with no blinding; adherence was monitored (81% tele-R, 78% trad-R) and exercise was supervised, but non-randomized allocation creates risk.
Two trad-R patients did not return for post-testing (25% attrition in control group), reducing analyzed n from 8 to 6 with no ITT analysis performed.
Objective physiological measures (CPET, spirometry) are robust; however, primary outcome (CFS-11) is self-reported and assessors were not blinded in this open-label study.
Study is registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05236478) and outcomes align with stated primary and secondary objectives.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. Post-treatment means for VO2max are calculated from baseline means plus reported absolute change (+3.8 for tele-R, +4.1 for trad-R); SD for change scores not explicitly reported. 2. Post-treatment per-arm means and SDs are not reported for MAP, VT1, FEV-1, 6-MWT, PetCO2 outcomes — only percent change ranges and time-effect p-values are given. Only baseline values (from Table 2) are extractable for these outcomes. 3. The paper reports percent improvements for MAP (22±17% tele-R vs 17±18% trad-R), VT1 (60±71% vs 41±33%), FEV-1 (14±12% vs 6±7%), 6-MWT (15±15% vs 6±4%) but these are percentage-change distributions, not absolute values; absolute endpoint values are not computable without baseline SD propagation. 4. Between-group effects are reported only as time effects (ANOVA), not as group differences with CIs — no between-group mean differences or CIs are available for any outcome. 5. VE/VCO2 slope data are described qualitatively (count of patients in ranges) with no per-arm means/SDs reported. 6. Delta PetCO2 rest/peak was not significantly modified (p=0.055) and is not extracted as a separate outcome. 7. Sex breakdown per arm not reported (only overall: 9 men, 8 women for n=17 randomized). 8. Several key aerobic outcome figures referenced (Figure 6) but numeric endpoint values are not extractable from figure descriptions in text.

domains.support: Allocation ratio was 4:2.7 (not 1:1) because 'efficacy of combination between umPEA-LUT and olfactory training was known'; randomization method not clearly described. Significant baseline age difference (36.7 vs 50.5 years) and imbalance in anosmia distribution between groups suggest inadequate randomization or allocation concealment.
Open-label design for patients (single-blind: outcome assessors blinded but patients and treating physicians aware of assignment). Adherence monitored by phone/electronic contact every 15 days.
No CONSORT flow diagram; no explicit reporting of dropouts, withdrawals, or losses to follow-up. Numbers completing treatment not clearly stated.

Olfactory testing performed by blinded assessors using validated Sniffin' Sticks identification test. Parosmia assessed by patient self-report using a previously published and validated questionnaire.
Trial registered (NCT04853836); primary and secondary outcomes appear consistent with stated aims.

subgroup_analyses.results_summary: In the control group, parosmia resolution was correlated with age (p=0.0007) and Sniffin' score at T0 (p=0.02). Authors note control group was younger (mean 50.5 vs 36.7 — note: control was actually older) and speculate spontaneous recovery in younger patients may explain parosmia improvement in control.

subgroup_analyses.outcome_name: Sniffin' Sticks Identification Score at T1
subgroup_analyses.results_summary: Multilinear regression showed that Sniffin' score at T0 was the only variable with statistically significant impact on T1 score in both treatment group (p<0.00001) and control group (p=0.009).

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. The paper reports 90-day (approximately 13-week) treatment; no post-treatment follow-up. 2. The control group had only 33 patients noted in some results paragraphs vs 36 randomized — slight discrepancy, possibly due to dropouts not explicitly described. 3. Between-group p-value for T1 Sniffin' score reported as HB p<0.05 (threshold, not exact). 4. Within-group change in treatment group: ANOVA p<0.0001, BH p<0.01; within control group: HB p>0.05 (not significant). 5. The paper notes baseline T0 difference between groups was not statistically significant (p>0.05) despite mean difference of 1.4 points. 6. Allocation ratio 4:2.7 is unusual and raises randomization concerns. 7. Age discrepancy in discussion: authors state 'control group included younger patients than treatment' but Table 1 shows treatment group mean age 36.7 vs control 50.5 — control is actually OLDER. This is an error in the paper. 8. Sniffin' Sticks identification only (not full TDI) was used. 9. No adverse events reported. 10. 'Stable' subgroup: 3 patients (3.2%) in treatment with mean 12.6±0.6 (CI 12-13); 3 patients (9.1%) in control — T1 score not reported for control stable subgroup.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. The paper reports mixed ANOVA group*time interaction F-statistics and partial eta-squared values but does NOT report mean differences with CIs for between-group comparisons; between-group effect_values were calculated as (arm1 post-mean minus arm2 post-mean). The interaction F-statistics and partial eta-squared are: MoCA F(1,24)=5.500, p=0.03, partial_eta2=0.186; Stroop-C F(1,24)=7.895, p=0.01, partial_eta2=0.248; RAVLT Sum F(1,22)=11.491, p=0.003, partial_eta2=0.343; RAVLT IR F(1,22)=4.744, p=0.04, partial_eta2=0.177; RAVLT DR F(1,22)=11.074, p=0.003, partial_eta2=0.335; TMT-A F(1,24)=3.926, p=0.059, partial_eta2=0.141; PHQ-9 F(1,23)=5.975, p=0.03, partial_eta2=0.206; Stroop W-C (executive) F(1,24)=4.243, p=0.05, partial_eta2=0.150. 2. Table 1 lists n=13 per group for demographics but text states experimental n=15 assigned, 14 completing, and Table 2 header shows n=13; the discrepancy for control group (16 assigned, 13 analyzed) is not fully explained. 3. The Stroop Words vs Colors between-group effect p-value (p=0.05) assigned to the Stroop Colors-Words interaction applies to the combined Stroop W-C subtest (executive function), not individually to Stroop-W. 4. Many outcome figures referenced in text but specific figure data not extractable from removed images. 5. Follow-up within-group mean differences reported in text for EG: MoCA MD=-2.38 SE=0.76 p=0.005; Stroop-C MD=-2.46 SE=0.96 p=0.018; TMT-A MD=-1.69 SE=0.576 p=0.007; RAVLT Sum MD=-11.07 SE=3.701 p=0.007; RAVLT IR MD=-6.38 SE=3.03 p=0.047; RAVLT DR MD=-7.308 SE=2.54 p=0.009; PHQ-9 MD=-6.00 SE=1.66 p=0.002 (these are pre-post within-EG differences, not between-group). 6. The paper labels MFE-Q as a primary measure but does not report a significant interaction for it. 7. Table 2 note: values are raw scores for MoCA, T scores for most attention/memory tests, and scaled scores for Stroop, TMT, DSC, ANIMALS. The between-group mean differences calculated here are therefore on heterogeneous scales and should be interpreted with caution.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. CRITICAL LIMITATION: Post-treatment (T1, T2, T3) per-arm means and SDs are NOT reported in any table. Table 2 only provides baseline (T0) values. The mixed-effects regression model coefficients (intercept, Age, BMI, Day, Time, Group, Time:Group) reported in Tables 3-6 are model coefficients, NOT per-arm means/SDs at each timepoint. The actual timepoint-specific outcome values appear only in Figures 2 and 3 (data only in figures for T1, T2, T3). Therefore, per-arm arm_results for T1, T2, T3 cannot be extracted and are omitted. Between-group effects are reported only as regression model Time:Group interaction coefficients (b values) with p<0.05 thresholds, not as mean differences with CIs, severely limiting quantitative extraction. The coefficient b=-0.119 for ST EC T0-T1 and b=-1.826 for SD OAP EC T1-T2 are Time:Group interaction terms from mixed effects models (Group A relative to Group B), not standard mean differences. Note also that the paper uses 'SD' ambiguously — both as 'Standard Deviation' (for oscillation measures) and as 'Mean Spatial Distance' parameter; extraction uses context to distinguish these. Table 1 reports age/BMI as median (IQR) format based on Wilcoxon test usage, but values are labeled as mean+SD in the results text; treated as mean+SD per text. Group B n=23 at T0 per Figure 1 caption but n=22 per text; used n=22 for analyzed sample in mixed models per text.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: This is a within-subjects waitlist controlled pilot study, not a parallel-group RCT. Arm 1 (intervention) and Arm 2 (waitlist control) represent the same 22 participants at different time periods; only 16 completed the post-intervention phase. The paired-samples t-tests reported compare waitlist (n=22) vs post-intervention (n=16) periods within participants. Cohen's d effect sizes were reported: Anxiety d=1.61, Rumination d=1.19, Social Connection d=1.22, Long-COVID Symptoms d=0.73. The t-statistics reported were: Anxiety t=8.03, Rumination t=5.84, Social Connection t=-6.10 (note negative sign for inverse direction), Long-COVID Symptoms t=3.65. Between-group effect values in this extraction are calculated as post-intervention mean minus waitlist mean. The study design does not permit standard between-group effect size calculation as typically defined in RCTs. The table in the paper had garbled formatting due to overlapping text from figure caption and table content; values were cross-referenced from text to verify. One-month follow-up data (n=6) had no means/SDs reported in the paper, only narrative description. Age range was 24-61 years with M=37.13, SD=9.44; all participants female and White British.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Table 2 reports postural stability data separated by sex within each arm (male n=15 and female n=11 for intervention; male n=8 and female n=12 for control), making it impossible to extract clean combined arm-level medians. The arm_results above use intervention group combined n=26 and control n=20 but the medians shown in the table are sex-stratified. The FRI 6-2 'after' values are not explicitly given in the table for all subgroups — the table row for FRI 6-2 appears incomplete with only some cells visible. Between-group effects use Glass's rank-biserial correlation R (reported as effect size), not SMD — the effect_measure field is set to 'smd' as the closest available schema option, but these are actually Mann-Whitney U Z statistics with R as rank-biserial correlation: OSI EO Z=-3.12, R=0.533; FRI 6-2 Z=-2.06, R=0.354; DOM2 Z=2.194, R=0.389; DOM3 Z=2.051, R=0.361; Q2 Z=3.309, R=0.535. WHOQOL-BREF domain means are averages of male and female subgroup means as reported (not weighted by n). Q1 and Q2 baseline means for control group are estimated from the table which shows male mean 4.1 and female mean 3.8 (Q1) and male 3.0, female 3.3 (Q2). Table 3 reports both mean and median for QOL outcomes. The n_randomized_total of 49 is inferred: 28 intervention (26 completed + 2 withdrew) + 20 control (originally 23 but 3 did not attend post-test — however text says 'control group: n=20' at final and mentions 3 did not attend post-test, so original control randomized was 23, but the text is ambiguous).

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. Lactate concentration per-session numeric data appears only in Figure 1 with no table or text values; only the overall group main effect F-statistic and p-value are reported (F=5.604, p=0.024). Distance covered data appears only in Figure 2 with no numeric values reported. 2. The overall age reported in the abstract (25.5 ± 7.1 years) conflicts with Table 1 which shows both groups have mean ages of ~46 years; the abstract value appears erroneous and per-arm values from Table 1 were used. The overall age/SD in baseline_demographics.overall reflects the abstract value but is likely a reporting error. 3. The 'Height' and 'Weight' values in Table 1 appear to be switched (height ~65cm, weight ~166cm), suggesting a data entry error in the paper. 4. Within-group p-values for Long-COVID pre vs. post: MFIS physical p=0.011, cognitive p=0.031, total p=0.009; SF-36 physical functioning p=0.001, social functioning p=0.011, bodily pain p=0.003, total SF-36 p=0.004. These are within-group comparisons only. 5. No between-group effect sizes (mean differences with CIs) were reported by the authors; all calculated between-group mean differences are from endpoint values only. 6. Two-way ANOVA group x time interaction results for SF-36 (F=4.632, p=0.002) and EQ-5D (F=4.340, p=0.014) indicate differential change between groups. 7. Non-randomized design with retrospective trial registration limits validity.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: The paper describes the control group as receiving 'no rehabilitation program' but the methods section text states 'the control group (who received a specific orofacial rehabilitation program)' — this appears to be a text error in the methods; the results clearly show the experimental group received the intervention and the control group did not. The between-group comparison for UPSIT was reported as percent change using Mann-Whitney test (non-parametric), while per-arm absolute scores were normally distributed by K-S test and analyzed with parametric tests within groups. Calculated mean difference for UPSIT endpoint (arm1 minus arm2): 33.40-30.50=2.90. Calculated mean difference for TST endpoint (arm1 minus arm2): 12.0-9.95=2.05. extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: CRITICAL DATA GAPS: Per-arm means and SDs are NOT reported for SF-36 subscales (all 8 subscales plus PCS and MCS) — data appears only in figures (Figure 2) as individual values with median lines; exact numeric values cannot be extracted. Per-arm means and SDs are also not reported for HADS, GAD-7, or PHQ-9 continuous scores — only Cohen's d effect sizes within each group are reported. Between-group effect sizes (Cohen's d) are reported only as within-group comparisons, NOT as between-group differences. No between-group p-values are reported for continuous outcomes except for HADS Anxiety binary outcome at 8 weeks (p<0.01, stated as '**'). Symptom duration reported as mean 51 (SD 27) weeks for rehabilitation group and 58 (SD 31) weeks for waiting list — converted to months as approximately 11.8 (SD 6.3) and 13.4 (SD 7.2) months respectively. The paper reports Cohen's d within the rehabilitation group for SF-36 outcomes (8 weeks): physical functioning=0.5, role physical=0.4, bodily pain=0.5, vitality=0.7, social functioning=0.6, role emotional=0.3, mental health=0.9, PCS=0.3, MCS=0.7. At 6 months: physical functioning=0.6, role physical=0.5, bodily pain=0.4, vitality=0.6, social functioning=0.6, role emotional=0.3, mental health=0.9, PCS=0.4, MCS=0.6. Waiting list within-group Cohen's d (8 weeks): physical functioning=0.5, social functioning=0.4, mental health=0.4. At 6 months: physical functioning=0.6, vitality=0.6, mental health=0.8. HADS within-group Cohen's d (TR): anxiety d=0.4 (p<0.01) at 8 weeks, d=0.6-0.7 (p<0.001) at 6 months; depression d=0.6-0.7 (p<0.001) at 8 weeks, 6 months. WL: depression only d=0.5-0.6 at 8 weeks (p<0.01) and 6 months (p<0.05). GAD-7 within-group TR: d=0.4 (p<0.01) at 8 weeks, d=0.3 (p<0.05) at 6 months; WL no improvement. PHQ-9 within-group TR: d=0.8 (p<0.001) at 8 weeks, d=0.5 (p<0.001) at 6 months; WL: d=0.6 (p<0.05) at 6 months only. ICF pain-related b-categories data presented only in Figure 3 as percentages — no extractable numeric means/SDs. SF-36 General Health showed no significant improvement in either group. IASP pain site data is in Supplemental Table S1 (not available in this text). N_randomized_total=116 inferred from 67+42+7 unaccounted (164 registered, 116 participated per text). Note: 164 registered, 116 participated and completed questionnaires at start, suggesting 48 did not meet criteria or withdrew before randomization. The 6-month follow-up had n=60 TR and n=21 WL. | Pass3 agent confirmed: no per-arm means/SDs for most outcomes, no CIs. Cohen's d within-group only. One significant binary finding: HADS anxiety 6% vs 24%, p<0.01.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. The Hedges' g values reported in the paper appear to represent within-group effect sizes (change from T1 to T2 within OMT arm), NOT between-group effect sizes; they have been extracted in between_group_effects as the best available effect measure since no true between-group effect statistics (mean differences with CIs) were reported for most outcomes. 2. Per-arm data for the sham group across most HRV outcomes (RMSSD, SDNN, LF, HF, TP, mean HR, mean RR, Stress Index) were NOT reported numerically in text or tables — only the OMT arm values and select sham LF/HF ratio values were given. Sham arm HRV data therefore not extractable. 3. The n values for OMT arm vary across outcomes (14–19 of 21 randomized), suggesting some missing measurements, but the paper provides no explanation for discrepancies. 4. The RMSSD g value at T3 (g=-0.55) has an asymmetric CI [-0.96, 0.18] crossing zero, indicating non-significant decline. 5. FAS was used for eligibility screening; post-intervention FAS values were mentioned as reduced but no numeric post-intervention data were provided. 6. Subjective dyspnea questionnaire (0–10 scale) and subjective well-being were listed as secondary outcomes but no quantitative results were reported. 7. The follow-up duration of 48 hours was converted to approximately 0.3 weeks. 8. The outlier table (Table 2) lists n=6 outliers but the text states n=5 participants with 4 in osteopathy and 2 in sham — a discrepancy noted in the paper itself. 9. LF/HF ratio results were only reported for the sham group (T2 vs T3 within-group change); OMT group LF/HF was stated to be 'statistically unchanged'. 10. Per-arm endpoint means and SDs at post-treatment and follow-up timepoints are NOT reported in text or tables for most outcomes — the paper reports only percentage change from baseline within each arm plus between-group t-tests and Cohen's d. Absolute endpoint values are only available at baseline. 2. The overall baseline mean for orgasmic function (3.43±1.2), sexual desire (3.52±1.12), intercourse satisfaction (5.74±1.9), and overall satisfaction (2.99±0.90) are stated as grand means across groups, not per-arm breakdowns. 3. Figure data (post-treatment and follow-up absolute scores) appears only in bar graphs with no accompanying tables; result_source set to 'not_reported' for these cells. 4. Cohen's d values are reported for within-arm pre-post comparisons and between-arm comparisons but are not extractable as standardized between-group effect sizes in the conventional meta-analytic sense (they appear to be reported for within-group change). 5. The TENS arm comparison for orgasmic function gives t=3.75, p=0.0006, Cohen's d=1.25 (53.6% improvement vs control); LLLT gives t=4.32, p=0.0001, Cohen's d=1.44 (69.5% improvement). 6. The intercourse satisfaction and overall satisfaction baseline means are reported as grand means across groups, not per arm individually. 7. EMG exploratory outcome data extracted in study but not included as formal outcome objects due to small, non-comparable subgroup and inability to attribute to specific treatment arms in follow-up. 8. Post-treatment (3-month) follow-up percentage changes for orgasmic function: LLLT +5.05%, TENS +4.43%, LLLT+TENS +5.17% (noted as not statistically reliable).

Table 2 CI for abdominal pain in PCIBS: lower bound listed as '-5.593' and '-5.008' in the extracted table — based on the table structure, PCIBS delta change CI 95% is (-7.560; -5.008) and Control delta change CI 95% is (-7.511; -5.593). extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. This is a 4-arm trial stratified by COVID severity (severe vs moderate), with a healthy donor control group (n=25, arm_id 5) that was not included in randomized arms as it received no intervention. 2. All cytokine biomarker data (IL-6, IL-8, IL-17A, IFN-gamma), nitrate/nitrite ratio, antioxidant activity (AOA), PMN ATP levels, and phagocytosis index quantitative data appear ONLY in figures (Figure 1, Figure 2, and referenced additional figures) with no tabulated numeric values extractable from text — these outcomes were noted as significant but numeric means/SDs were not reported in text. Outcomes omitted due to data-only-in-figures: IL-6, IL-8, IL-17A, IFN-gamma plasma levels, plasma nitrate/nitrite ratio, antioxidant activity, PMN ATP content, phagocytosis index (%), intracellular bacterial killing (%). 3. The Borg scale is labeled 1-10 but Group 3 baseline values (10.8) exceed this range — likely the scale used differs or values represent a different metric (possibly a modified Borg or dyspnea visual analogue scale); values extracted as reported verbatim. 4. Table 2 had extensive merged/duplicate rows with the same values appearing for multiple answer score levels (e.g., '2-great' and '1-moderate' rows show identical means); only one set of values per question item was extracted. 5. ECG data reported as counts at two time points (30-40 days and 50-60 days post-discharge), corresponding to baseline and end-of-trial respectively. 6. No primary outcome was designated; paper lacks trial registration. 7. Oral-nasal-pharyngeal microbiota data not tabulated quantitatively. 8. A 5th group (healthy donors, n=25) served as a normative reference and was not randomized; excluded from arm-level extraction. 9. The Borg score for severe COVID groups is presented such that improvement = score increases (counterintuitive direction); values extracted verbatim. Higher Borg score in this paper's context may indicate improved exercise tolerance rather than worse dyspnea — this is ambiguous from text; higher_is_better set to false as Borg score conventionally measures dyspnea/exertion.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: CRITICAL LIMITATION: This paper reports all outcomes collapsed across both arms combined (overall pre vs. post), not disaggregated by experimental vs. control arm. Per-arm means, SDs, and Ns are NOT reported for any outcome. The arm_id fields for arm_results are set to null to reflect this. The between_group_effects p-values reported are for within-group (pre vs. post overall) paired tests, NOT between-arm comparisons; no experimental vs. control between-group statistics are reported anywhere in the paper. This severely limits the trial's usability for meta-analysis. Table 1 reports overall pre/post for 1-min STS (26.75±5.04 vs 28.75±5.6, p=0.002119), Fatigue NRS (2.72±1.33 vs 2.26±1.19, p=0.0223), and L-Test (19.18±5.08 vs 18.24±3.64, p=0.006627). Table 2 reports overall pre/post hand grip strength for right (14.27±4.39 vs 14.35±4.75, within p=0.8722) and left (14.05±4.58 vs 14.0±4.45, within p=0.8965) with changes of 0.08±2.7 and 0.06±2.37 respectively (between-hand change comparison p=0.9717). Some data appear only in figures (Figures 1-4) with no additional numerical values beyond those in tables. The conclusion text contains an apparent error: it states 'subjects took less time in pretest compared to post test' for the STS, but the data show higher count post-test (improvement), suggesting a narrative error. N=30 total but per-arm allocation not stated.

The between_group_effects calculated here represent T1(OFS) minus T1(Placebo); however the actual test statistic was a paired crossover comparison. SF-36 and ESS numeric data appear only in figures (Figures 1-4) — no tabular values reported; result_source set to not_reported for these outcomes. Neutrophils, lymphocytes, monocytes, eosinophils, platelets, creatinine, eGFR, azotemia, and albuminuria from Table 1 are not extracted as separate outcome objects due to output size constraints — all were non-significant. Body composition parameters (Table 3) beyond weight and BMI omitted for brevity — all were non-significant. Heart rate from Table 4 omitted — non-significant. The study reports 4 time-points (T0, T1, T2, T3) but only T0 and T1 data are tabulated; T2 and T3 data not reported numerically.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: Paper is in Russian with an English abstract. The § symbol in original text represents ±. Treatment duration inferred as approximately 3 weeks (18 daily sessions of 30-40 min). The paper states p>0.05 at baseline (groups comparable) and p<0.05 at end of treatment (intervention superior), but only threshold p-values are provided, not exact values. The 'Depression Questionnaire' (Oprosnik depressivnogo sostoyaniya) is a Russian instrument not identical to standard Western scales; scoring: <40=neurotic spectrum, 40-60=diagnostic uncertainty, >60=high depression. PSM-25 scoring: ≤99=low stress, 100-125=moderate, >125=high. Control group also rested at park-hotel Ershovo, providing an environmental confound. Age differed substantially between arms (intervention ~42 years vs control ~51 years), suggesting possible non-random allocation. The between_group_effects p_value field uses p<0.05 threshold (p_value_exact=false). EEG alpha-rhythm power data (effective training time improvement of 124.4s, continuous retention improvement of 23.3s) mentioned in text but no per-arm quantitative table provided, so not extracted as formal outcomes. The overall mean age of 42.25±2.59 stated in paper likely refers to the intervention group only despite being presented as overall in the abstract.

Classified as quasi-experimental. 2. Age values reported as mean±SEM (not SD): MRQ 57.8±2.5, MR 58.7±2.64, Control 51.3±2.3 — these SEM values are stored in age_sd fields but are actually SEM. 3. All biomarker results in Tab.2 are mean±SEM (not SD) per paper methods section ('expressed as mean±standard error of mean'). SE values stored in se fields accordingly. 4. The control group (arm 3) is healthy volunteers, not a post-COVID comparator group; only one timepoint for controls. 5. Clinical symptom questionnaire was completed by subsets: MRQ n=20 (of 22 enrolled) and MR n=10 (of 14 enrolled). Symptom outcomes use these smaller analyzed Ns. 6. The plasma beta-carotene MR2 SE value appears unusually large (0.171) possibly a typo for 0.017 in the original table — extracted verbatim. 7. Between-group effects for biomarkers are not reported by the paper; calculated mean differences (arm1 minus arm2 at endpoint) provided where meaningful. 8. Symptom outcomes (outcomes 13-16) are a subset — additional symptom data extracted for: difficulty breathing, chills, heart palpitations, respiratory support with O2, weakness, malaise, GIT problems, diarrhea, chest pain, headache, weight loss, hearing impairment — omitted from outcomes array to manage output size but all raw counts available in Tab.1. 9. extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. This is a doctoral thesis document, not the final published journal article. The full results tables (Table 2.1 Baseline Characteristics and Table 2.2 Efficacy End Points) and figures (Figure 2.2, Figure 2.3) referenced in the text are listed in a table of contents but their actual numeric content is not present in the provided text excerpt — the document appears truncated before the Results section tables. Consequently, per-arm means, SDs, and sample sizes for all outcomes are unavailable and set to null. Only summary statistics and effect measures reported in the abstract/summary narrative could be extracted. The paper is a crossover trial; the between-group effects reported represent treatment vs. control period comparisons accounting for the crossover design. No carry-over or period effects were detected per the authors. The document mentions a safety committee and adverse events section (section 11) but no AE data was present in the extracted text. The exact cognitive measurement instruments used for 'cognitive capabilities' (p=0.014) and 'cognitive performance' (p=0.036) are listed in abbreviations (MOCA, TMT-A) but which p-value corresponds to which instrument is ambiguous. The 22 long COVID symptoms were assessed but only 7 reached significance; the remaining 15 symptoms are not individually listed with RR values in the provided text. The full published journal version (European Heart Journal, 2024) would contain complete tabular data.
