extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. Table 2 uses the format 'mean±SD' (the § symbol in the source text represents ±). The table also reports Cohen's d effect sizes with 95% CIs for within-group pre-to-post changes and between-group comparison at post-test; these were extracted as interaction p-values for between_group_effects. The total row in Table 2 reports pooled means across both groups (e.g., SpO2 pre 97.9±0.8, post 98.1±0.7; FVC pre 3.1±0.4, post 3.5±0.3; FEV1 pre 2.6±0.5, post 2.8±0.4; FEV1/FVC pre 82.5±12.9, post 79.4±11.8; PEF pre 4.1±1.3, post 4.7±1.4; MVV pre 53.3±11.1, post 71.5±11.1; MRf pre 81.5±24.5, post 93.4±18.3; MVt pre 0.7±0.4, post 0.8±0.3) — these total values were not extracted as separate arm results. The between_group_effects p-values used are the interaction effect (Time x Treatment) F-test p-values from the split-plot RM ANOVA, which are the most appropriate indicator of differential group change. The paper reports Cohen's d effect sizes per arm (pre-to-post within each group) but not standardized between-group effect sizes; per-arm Cohen's d values are: SpO2: control=0.08 [CI -0.28,0.44], exercise=-0.49 [-0.87,-0.11]; FVC: control=-0.66 [-1.05,-0.26], exercise=-0.70 [-1.10,-0.30]; FEV1: control=0.01 [-0.38,0.37], exercise=-0.66 [-1.05,0.26]; FEV1/FVC: control=0.47 [0.09,0.84], exercise=-0.23 [-0.59,0.13]; PEF: control=0.00 [-0.35,0.36], exercise=-0.67 [-1.07,-0.27]; MVV: control=-0.97 [-1.40,-0.53], exercise=-1.29 [-1.77,-0.79]; MRf: control=-0.24 [-0.60,0.12], exercise=-0.56 [-0.94,-0.17]; MVt: control=-0.29 [-0.65,0.08], exercise=-0.01 [-0.37,0.35]. Note: FEV1/FVC baseline differed significantly between groups (p=0.039), which is a baseline imbalance. The table also reports between-group effect sizes at posttest: SpO2=-0.79 [-1.31,-0.26]; FVC=-0.32 [-0.83,0.18]; FEV1=-0.82 [-1.35,-0.29]; FEV1/FVC=-0.58 [-1.10,-0.06]; PEF=-0.80 [-1.33,-0.27]; MVV=-0.13 [-0.63,0.37]; MRf=-0.53 [-1.04,-0.01]; MVt=0.47 [-0.04,0.98].

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: MD was garbled, used PDF text. This paper is primarily a systems immunology/biomarker analysis of the STOP-PASC RCT, NOT the main efficacy trial report. Primary clinical efficacy outcomes (patient-reported outcomes comparing NMV/r vs PBO/r) are reported in a prior publication and only referenced here. No per-arm means/SDs or between-group effect sizes are reported for the core PRO symptom outcomes in this paper. The main quantitative data extracted are biomarker outcomes: LCS score change from baseline (p-values only, no means/SDs in figures), microclotting data (means/SDs from Table S4), and counts of differentially expressed proteins. Most proteomic outcome data appears only in figures (volcano plots, heatmaps, box plots) without tabulated values. Table S5 is truncated in the provided text. The paper reports that the mean protracted LC illness duration was >16 months but no per-arm time-since-infection data is provided. The LCS score p-values (0.1208 for day 15, 0.969 for week 10) were read from Figure 4G. Omitted outcomes (data only in figures): anti-SARS-CoV-2 antibody levels per arm over time, individual pathway summary scores, autoantibody prevalence by antigen, individual protein associations with PROs.

Table 2 labels 'Control' for ATR group (arm_id=2) and 'Intervention' for STR group (arm_id=1); arm_id assignments maintained consistently throughout extraction. Between-group p-values in Table 2 are from mixed-model effects across all timepoints (not timepoint-specific), so they are assigned to timepoint_id=2 (end of treatment) as the primary comparison point. No between-group CIs were provided for any outcome. The n_analyzed values (17 STR, 14 ATR) are ITT population counts from Table 1 baseline which matches the analyzed sample after ITT imputation. Note: 44 randomized but only 31 in ITT analysis table (Table 1 shows n=31 total); paper states 23 STR and 21 ATR randomized but 17 STR and 14 ATR in final ITT analysis. Patient-Specific Functional Scale was pre-registered but excluded from analysis due to data collection errors.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1) This paper reports only a per-protocol subgroup analysis; the primary ITT analysis per the Statistical Analysis Plan is stated to be reported elsewhere, substantially limiting extractable between-group effect estimates. 2) Cohen's d effect sizes were reported for within-arm changes (VAS active: d=0.939; sham: d=0.513; placebo: d=0.384; FIS Total active: d=0.544; FIS Social active: d=0.426; FIS Physical active: d=0.849; FIS Cognitive active: d=0.339; TI_PeriphFatigue active: d=-0.531) but not extracted into structured fields as they are within-arm pre-post effect sizes, not between-group. 3) Per-arm means and SDs at baseline and endpoint (not just change scores) are not reported; only change-from-baseline means and SDs were stated for VAS and FIS Total; other FIS subscores lacked change score SDs. 4) Many quantitative electrophysiological outcome data (TMS measures, StartReact, GSR, HRV, SSRT) appear only in spider plot figures (Figure 5) with no tabular values — marked as not_reported in arm_results and omitted from outcomes to manage output size. 5) Baseline demographics broken down by arm are not reported; only overall per-protocol cohort demographics given (N=59, 45 females, age 49.8±10.2 years). 6) FACIT-F questionnaire is mentioned as collected but no results are reported. 7) Adverse events not fully broken down by arm; the text provides partial information allowing only approximate arm attribution. 8) The sham group crossover VAS improvement (p=0.009) and FIS total (p=0.044) after switching to active are noted as trends not surviving multiple comparisons correction.

domains.support: Randomization via SAS 9.4 with block size 6, 1:1 ratio; allocation implemented by unblinded research pharmacists; sequence generation appears adequate.
Double-blind design with identical-appearing pills; however, 4 participants received COVID-19 vaccine during the study and adherence was not formally assessed.
14 of 32 randomized participants (43.75%) did not complete the study; only 18 completers analyzed (per-protocol, not ITT); blood samples available for only 13 of 18 completers.
Symptom outcomes were self-reported via REDCap survey without validated instruments; biomarker outcomes (omega-3 index, AA:EPA ratio) measured by spot blood sample.
Study pre-registered on ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05121766) and registered with FDA (IND #157250); stated outcomes align with reported results.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. Symptom outcomes measured categorically (never had / resolved at week 1-2 / week 3 / week 4 / still experiencing); OR reported in text for 'still experiencing' vs resolved/never. Events for binary outcomes extracted from 'I still experience this symptom' row. 2. Table 1 demographics show n=32 at baseline but completers table (Table 2) shows placebo n=10, omega-3 n=8 (18 total); demographics table appears to reflect all 32 randomized. 3. Age in Table 2 (completers) shows placebo mean 50.3 SD 13.2 (text) vs Table showing median 55.5 (24,66) for placebo and median 52.5 (36,62) for supplement — some discrepancy in table headers vs text values resolved by using text-stated values. 4. The difference in omega-3 index for placebo is reported as -0.373 (SD=0.551) meaning week12 - baseline = negative, i.e., week 12 was higher; sign convention appears inverted in paper (baseline minus week12). For AA:EPA ratio difference, values reported as positive meaning baseline minus week12 (reduction). Extracted as reported verbatim. 5. For the calculated between-group mean difference in omega-3 change: intervention change mean (-2.23) minus placebo change mean (-0.373) = -1.857, indicating greater increase in omega-3 index in supplement group. 6. For AA:EPA ratio change: intervention change (11.4) minus placebo change (3.06) = 8.34, indicating greater reduction in AA:EPA ratio in supplement group. 7. Table 1 (demographics) column headers not fully captured in paper text; values 47.3 (12.2) and 46.4 (9.78) appear in table but text states placebo 50.3 SD 13.2 and treatment 49.8 SD 10.9 — these likely represent all-enrolled vs completers. Baseline demographics per arm reflect completers (n=10 placebo, n=8 supplement) using text-stated values. 8. CONSORT flow diagram referenced but image not readable; dropout numbers inferred from text.

domains.support: Randomization used closed-envelope method, which is described. However, the groups had significant baseline differences (WHO severity, ICU stay, O2 requirement, 6MWT distance, resting HR, SF-36 subscales), suggesting possible inadequate allocation concealment or insufficient stratification.
Open-label design with no blinding of participants or providers. Both groups received the same co-interventions (breathing, UE strengthening), but unblinded delivery could introduce performance bias.

13 of 76 randomized patients did not complete the study (76 randomized, 63 analyzed), but reasons for dropout per arm are not reported. The SF-36 social function posttreatment value for LIIT group appears missing from Table 2.
Outcome assessors were not blinded. Functional and patient-reported outcomes (mMRC, Borg, SF-36, HADS) are susceptible to performance and detection bias in an open-label trial.
No pre-registration or protocol publication is mentioned. Primary outcome is not formally declared; multiple outcomes tested without multiplicity correction.

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. Table 2 has a missing posttreatment value for SF-36 social function in the LIIT group (arm_id=2, timepoint_id=2) — the cell appears blank/cut off in the paper. 2. The treatment duration was 15 sessions at 3-5x/week, equating to approximately 3-5 weeks; 5 weeks used as upper estimate for follow-up duration. 3. Table 3 (changes from pre- to posttreatment) was cut off in the provided text and could not be fully extracted — between-group change scores and their p-values for outcomes such as mMRC, resting HR, and 6MWT (reported as significantly higher in LIIT) are not available as numeric values with SDs. 4. The paper reports that 'changes in mMRC, resting heart rate, and 6MWT distance were significantly higher in the LIIT group' but the actual change score values are in Table 3 which was truncated. 5. BMI data in Table 1 appears garbled (values shown as 29.5±4.84 for CT FFM and 58.66±7.91 for LIIT FFM — likely the BMI row and FFM row are merged/misaligned in the extracted table). Values interpreted based on context: BMI CT=29.5±4.84, FFM CT=59.88±10.54, BMI LIIT=29.37±5.42, FFM LIIT=58.66±7.91. 6. Resting HR at baseline in Table 1 shows CT=90.7±12.52 but Table 2 shows CT pretreatment=89.55±12.81 — slight discrepancy, Table 2 values used for pre/post analysis. Similarly LIIT baseline HR: Table 1=99.1±17.43, Table 2=99.47±17.23; Table 2 values used. 7. No formal primary outcome was declared. 8. Adverse events were not systematically reported. 9. Omitted from outcomes extraction: resting RPE (only median/range, not consistently reported with SDs), 6th-minute HR and RPE during 6MWT (reported with means and SDs in Table 2 but excluded to stay within output limits), minimum SpO2 during exercise test, maximum HR/BP/RPE/MBD during exercise test, oxygen supplementation requirement (binary outcome — see Table 2 for per-arm proportions).

domains.support: Randomization sequence generated by uninvolved nurse using sealedenvelope.com with minimization to balance prognostic factors; allocation concealment achieved via central online tool.
Open-label design; no blinding of participants or providers. Participants asked to refrain from other mindfulness-based interventions during study period, and treatment adherence was monitored.
5 participants lost in intervention arm at 6-month follow-up (dropout rate 9.6%); 7 additional lost in control arm by 12 months. No ITT analysis performed — completers only analyzed.
All outcomes are self-reported via validated instruments (BPI-SF, HADS, ISI); no blinding of participants to allocation, introducing potential response bias.
Trial prospectively registered at ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05815693) before enrollment. Primary and secondary outcomes pre-specified in protocol.

subgroup_analyses.results_summary: No gender differences emerged in benefits of MBSR for any outcome (pain, anxiety, depression, insomnia, concurrent psychopathology).

extraction_metadata.extractor_notes: 1. The paper does not report baseline (pre-MBSR) outcome scores — all reported values are from 6-month and 12-month post-MBSR timepoints. No baseline means/SDs available for BPI-SF, HADS, or ISI. Weeks_from_randomization for the two timepoints are estimated as ~32 weeks (8 weeks treatment + ~6 months follow-up) and ~58 weeks (8 weeks treatment + ~12 months follow-up). 2. HADS anxiety and depression mean scores are reported in text/Figure 3 but SDs are not provided for these continuous scores. ISI continuous means (9, 13.6 at 6 months; 9.1, 11.1 at 12 months) are also reported without SDs. T-statistics are given for HADS-A (t=-3.636, t=-5.167) and HADS-D (t=-2.823, t=-2.458) and ISI (t=-8.801, t=-3.569) but not CIs. 3. The insomnia categorical outcome (absence of insomnia 53.2% vs 30.4%) was reported with chi-square statistic (x=4.944, p=.026) — this appears to be the chi-square value not the ISI mean score as stated in the abstract. 4. The abstract states insomnia score '53.2 vs 30.4' which matches the categorical percentages in Table 2 (not ISI continuous scores), suggesting the abstract conflated percentage data with score data. 5. Control group n at 12 months is 43 per Table 2 (not 46), consistent with 3 additional dropouts noted in limitations. 6. Baseline demographic table shows n=93 for analyzed population but randomization was 105 total (52 IG + 53 CG). The 12 missing patients (5 IG + 7 CG) are the dropouts. 7. The paper uses 'psychoeducation' as the label for the MBSR intervention in the abstract methods section but the intervention is clearly MBSR throughout.
